title: Annotatio III §.X (5)(1)–(2): Removes the material Sign; turns Signatum into the Sacrament of Signatum itself
pass_a_gloss: (1.) That it removes from the Eucharist the Material Sign, the other essential part of a sacrament — namely bread and wine — only the accidents of these substances remaining, void as of all substantiality, in the Pontificians’ sentence, so also of Materiality. (2) That it changes the Signatum of the Eucharistic Sacrament (namely Christ’s Body and Blood) into the very Sacrament of the Signatum of Christ’s Body and Blood.
pass_b_english: (1) It removes the material Sign — bread and wine — leaving only accidents, void of substantiality and (on their view) of materiality too.
(2) It turns the Signatum (Christ’s body and blood) into the sacrament of that Signatum itself — sign and thing collapse.
source_text: (1.) Quòd Signum Materiale, alteram sacramenti partem essentialem, ex Eucharistia submovet, panem nempe & vinum, solis remanentibus harum substantiarum accidentibus, ut substantialitate omni, ex sententia Pontificiorum, ita & Materialitate, casssis. (2) Quòd Signatum Sacramenti Eucharistici (Corpus nempe & Sanguinem Christi) in ipsum Signati Sacramentum Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, commutat.

lemmas.gloss: changes into the Sacrament of the Signatum itself
